name: Hungarian
script: Latin with extra letters: á, é, í, ó, ö, ő, ú, ü, ű, and the letters cs, dz, dzs, gy, ly, ny, sz, ty, zs; left to right
basis: University beginner Hungarian (S.O.S. Magyar 1 as taught at Pécs; Corvinus Hungarian for Beginners I)
src: University of Pécs: Hungarian for Engineers 1 (SZE084AN, autumn 2023) weekly schedule with grammar and S.O.S. Magyar 1 pages
Corvinus University (CEA syllabus): Hungarian for Beginners I weekly topics and grammar
elon.io: Hungarian grammar A1 learner path (a grammar website's path, not a course syllabus)
note: The order follows the Pécs schedule (alphabet, articles, there is / isn't, pronouns and 'to be', question words, vowel harmony, numbers, -ban / -ben, present conjugation, -on / -en / -ön, ordinals, accusative -t and plurals, hova / hol / honnan, postpositions, past of 'to be', -val / -vel) with Corvinus for ordering food and directions. Putting vowel harmony in stage 1, definite conjugation, -ik verbs, possessive endings, 'have' with van / nincs, and szeret + -ni are common course practice and my own judgment; all titles are mine.
hardest: Long vs short vowels (ö / ő, ü / ű) and the spellings s, sz, cs, zs, gy, ny
Vowel harmony: most endings have two or three forms
Definite vs indefinite conjugation: látok or látom

items: Vowels: short and long, ö / ő, ü / ű
Consonants: s, sz, cs, zs, gy, ny, ty and double letters
Introducing yourself: Anna vagyok, amerikai vagyok
Vowel harmony: back and front words
No 'is' in the third person: A ház nagy
Questions: ki, mi, hol, milyen, hány
There is, there isn't: van, nincs, and itt, ott, ez, az
Days and telling the time: Hány óra van?, fél három
My and your: a házam, a házad
Having: Van egy kutyám, Nincs autóm
Was and will be: volt, lesz
Likes: szeret, and the infinitive -ni (szeretek úszni)
